1.t: Harvest festival: Snowball discussion on why and how Pongal is kept
1.y: In pairs, then fours, then sixes, students share why, when and how Pongal is celebrated. The guide tags civic literacy and cross-cultural understanding here.

1.t: Tamil and me: Discussing why Tamil marks community identity, and Tamil-related jobs
1.y: Groups discuss how and why Tamil is seen as a mark of identity and how to learn of jobs using Tamil. Partial: one community's angle, no contrasting view is set.

3.t: Water management: Why Singapore gets water from abroad, and what each level can do
3.y: Pairs answer why Singapore draws water from Malaysia and how it stores rain, then say what individuals, families, schools and the nation can do to protect water.

3.t: Water management: Discussing challenges people faced during water rationing
3.y: Students discuss the difficulties people likely met during past rationing, then do a listening task. The guide tags civic literacy and global awareness here.

3.t: Water management: Discussing Singapore's water-saving challenges and journey
3.y: Pairs and groups discuss challenges Singapore faced in saving water using 1963 photos. Only Singapore's own story is covered, so it is one perspective.

1.t: New beginnings: Building one story as a group, then revising it from comments
1.y: Groups build one story using SCAMPER, present it, then revise the story in light of classmates' comments and questions, taking in suggestions.

1.t: Tamil and me: Group talk with cards for raising questions and differing views
1.y: Each member shares a view; cards signal a wish to question or offer another view, within groups and when other groups report back.

1.t: Tamil and me: Text message congratulating a younger sibling before a contest
1.y: Students reply to a sibling entering a speech contest, first with praise and then tips on preparing, after imagining what more they would advise.

3.t: Water management: Role-playing people hit by water rationing
3.y: After discussing the hardships people likely faced during rationing, students may act as those people. An optional extension task.

3.t: Water management: Speaking as a story character about how he was affected
3.y: One or two students imagine themselves as a poor character from the short story and tell the class how brief kindness affected him.

2.t: Goals: Working out what to do in three life situations
2.y: After reading situations, students think through and write a response to a third, then compare it with a model answer and comment. The guide tags responsible decision-making.

2.t: Goals: Deciding how a story ends, then sharing how they solved similar school problems
2.y: Students decide and may act out what a character would choose on a group-work problem, then share similar problems of their own and how they solved them.

3.t: The internet: Comparing early posters with online posters
3.y: Students compare the make-up of two or three posters and talk about how early printed posters differ from today's online posters, before making their own.

3.t: Water management: Comparing two pictures of the Singapore River
3.y: Students discuss what is alike and what differs between two pictures of the river across time. An extension task; it does not go on to a changed approach.

2.t: Email reply: Replying to a friend's email for set purposes
2.y: Students read a friend's email and write a reply covering each purpose set, such as sharing experience or giving advice, in a friendly register. One-way writing to a named reader.

2.t: Oral exam: Answering examiner questions on a video
2.y: After a short video, students answer examiner questions: their reaction or experience, what they suggest, and whether they agree with a given view, giving reasons. Spoken, with the examiner.

2.t: Goals: Writing a friendly email on skills to develop and getting a reply with comments
2.y: Students email a classmate about two skills they want to grow; the classmate replies and comments on the email's parts and the pledges. Audience and purpose are set.

2.t: Goals: Performing a short play showing a chosen life skill
2.y: Groups pick a saying and perform a play showing that life skill; classmates name the saying it shows. The task is one way, from performers to audience.

3.t: Slide presentation: Giving reasons, an experience and benefits on a set topic
3.y: Students prepare 3 to 4 slides and notes on a set topic, giving reasons, an experience and benefits, and present to the class. One-way presentation.

3.t: The internet: Making a poster on the uses of computers
3.y: Students study sample posters, then make their own poster on a set topic, using the poster's parts for its purpose. The task is one way, aimed at poster viewers.

3.t: Water management: Telling a water story from the Author's Chair and taking questions
3.y: A group member presents a story on the need for water; classmates comment and ask questions, then the story is revised. The audience is peers.

1.t: New beginnings: Telling a group story from the Author's Chair and taking questions
1.y: After building a story in a group with SCAMPER, one member presents it; classmates comment and ask questions, and the story is revised. The audience is peers.

1.t: Harvest festival: Making a brochure on harvest festivals abroad from collected information
1.y: Students collect information and make a brochure following a sample, then show it to the class. The task is one way, aimed at readers of the brochure.

3.t: Water management: Looking up online the 1963 water pictures before class
3.y: Students find details online about the textbook's water-supply pictures and bring what they gathered to the discussion. A light, set search.

1.t: Harvest festival: Researching how three countries celebrate harvest festivals
1.y: In groups students use web pages to find which countries hold harvest festivals, pick three and find out how each is celebrated, before making a brochure.

1.t: Tamil and me: Searching a Tamil news site for what learning Tamil offers them
1.y: Groups use the Tamil Murasu e-page to answer questions on what they gain from Tamil and where to find Tamil news, giving evidence for their views.

1.t: New beginnings: K-W-L sheet on what they know and want to know about secondary school
1.y: Students write what they already know and want to know about secondary school, share it, then check whether the reading answers their own questions.

2.t: Keeping healthy: Filling a K-W-L sheet on food
2.y: Students note what they know about food from the lesson pictures, add what they want to know, and share before the reading.

1.t: Tamil and me: Group summary of findings on using Tamil, with questions from the class
1.y: One member of each group sums up the group's ideas for the class; classmates add views and ask questions.

2.t: Goals: Setting a goal for the year from a chosen quality
2.y: Each student picks one quality and turns it into a goal for the year, drawn or written in the textbook. An extension task.

2.t: Goals: Writing personal pledges for skills to grow and how to build them
2.y: Students write down skills or qualities they want to develop as pledges, choose two and explain why and how they could grow them, sharing with a peer.

1.t: New beginnings: Revising a story after classmates' comments and questions
1.y: Students improve their story draft using the comments and questions raised when it was read from the Author's Chair.

3.t: Water management: Revising a water story after classmates' comments
3.y: Students improve their story draft using the comments and questions raised when it was read from the Author's Chair.

2.t: Goals: Pairs asking each other why and how about qualities they like
2.y: One partner explains qualities they like and the other asks why and how, then pairs choose one they both like and show it to the class.

3.t: The internet: Reflecting on how they help family members use technology
3.y: Students discuss which family members use technology and how they help grandparents or parents with it. Reflection through discussion only.

1.t: New beginnings: Class bingo matching classmates who gave the same answers
1.y: Students share their likes and thoughts with classmates, note who answered alike and discuss in pairs, getting to know the new class; this is a short opening activity.

2.t: Keeping healthy: Sharing own habits for staying healthy and why some skip them
2.y: Students share what they do to stay healthy and give reasons why some classmates do not follow healthy habits; discussion only, with no tracking or planning.

terms.1: Friendship · Hobbies · Protecting the environment · WA1
terms.2: Kings of Tamil Nadu · Yesterday, today, tomorrow · AA · Oral
terms.3: Financial literacy · Youth and society · WA3

1.t: Friendship: Fishbowl discussion of how to choose friends
1.y: An inner circle discusses questions with no set answer while the rest listen; those holding differing views swap in and put them to the group.

2.t: Newspaper article: Group drafting and peer editing
2.y: Groups peer-edit the article together and share a single video presentation, taking in each other's suggestions to finish a common product. Evidence of disagreement handling is limited.

1.t: Hobbies: Comparing a print newspaper report with an online one
1.y: Students compare news in a home newspaper with online news, note what is alike and different, and post these online, before writing their own report.

2.t: Kings of Tamil Nadu: Comparing old kings' duties with monarchies today
2.y: As a lead-in to reading, students discuss what kings once had to do and compare it with monarchy in other countries now. Short, and not tied to a changed view.

2.t: Yesterday, today, tomorrow: How living on the moon would differ from living on Earth
2.y: After reading, students discuss and share differences between life on the moon and on Earth. An imagined context; they do not go on to a changed approach.

3.t: Financial literacy: Comparing old postal methods with present ones
3.y: Students discuss how past postal methods compare with those of today as a lead-in to writing an email. A short lead-in comparison.

1.t: Protecting the environment: Weighing why Singapore should become a city in nature
1.y: Students read Singapore's park plans before class, discuss what the government plans, and say whether the change is needed and what it gains. The guide tags civic literacy.

1.t: Protecting the environment: Could Singapore face the same risk, and what can be done?
1.y: After reading about environmental risk, students say whether Singapore could face it, why, and what they and other countries can do. Whole-class questions.

1.t: Protecting the environment: News on Singapore's old street traders and recyclers
1.y: Students may gather reports and pictures of past street traders and recycling collectors into a class display, then talk over how Singapore has changed.

2.t: Kings of Tamil Nadu: Explaining what Singapore's flag stands for
2.y: Students build on primary-school knowledge and work out what the colours, moon and stars on the flag represent. National identity, a single view; the guide names this goal.

3.t: Youth and society: Taking opposing stances on whether youths should join community groups
3.y: In shark and dolphin groups students argue for or against youths joining community organisations; the guide aims for students to meet different viewpoints. Stances are assigned.

3.t: Youth and society: Discussing news stories on youth helping the community
3.y: Groups choose a news report on youth solving community problems and discuss the problem and the solution.

2.t: Yesterday, today, tomorrow: Weighing solutions on a decision form and reaching their own
2.y: For a question from the reading, students list solutions, the gains and the problems to expect, then write their own decision and share the form with the class.

1.t: Email reply: Giving advice to a friend who wrote about a problem
1.y: Students read a friend's email about a situation and write a reply that gives advice and reasons. One-way writing to a named reader.

1.t: Protecting the environment: Speaking as the forest, tree or sea to the class
1.y: Students take the role of a forest, tree or sea and tell the class why it matters and what harms it, then assess their own speaking. One way, aimed at classmates.

2.t: Oral exam: Answering examiner questions on a video
2.y: After a short video, students answer examiner questions: their reaction or experience, what they suggest, and whether they agree with a given view, giving reasons. Spoken, with the examiner.

2.t: Newspaper article and video: Telling a school community member's story
2.y: Students interview a real person, then convey the story in a newspaper article and a recorded presentation for readers and viewers. Largely one-way presentation to an audience.

2.t: Yesterday, today, tomorrow: Creating an online advertisement for a robot company
2.y: Students make an online ad for an imagined robot maker, choosing a title, buyer group, pictures and contact details to suit the audience. One way.

3.t: Youth and society: Finding what other community organisations do to involve youth
3.y: Students find other Singapore community organisations and what each has done to bring in young people, then share. Partial: they list efforts rather than compare roles.

1.t: Protecting the environment: Gathering material on past street traders for a class display
1.y: Students look up recycling collectors online before class and may gather reports and pictures of such traders for a class display. A set topic.

1.t: Hobbies: Finding online which hobbies did not exist in 1980s Singapore
1.y: Pairs compare their own hobbies with the pictures, search online for hobbies absent in 1980s Singapore, then share with classmates; a small, narrow search.

2.t: Interview: Finding out a school community member's story first-hand
2.y: Students interview a real person live in Tamil, ask their own questions and make sense of the replies to build the article. They find out first-hand.

2.t: Kings of Tamil Nadu: Searching online for missing facts about the Tamil kings
2.y: Students read up beforehand, discuss in groups, search online for facts that were missing, write them down and share with a partner.

2.t: Yesterday, today, tomorrow: Finding the source of a floppy disk image online
2.y: Students search online for the origin of the pictured floppy disk and use what they found to answer the textbook questions, then share with the class.

3.t: Youth and society: Researching community organisations and their youth efforts
3.y: Students look up other community organisations and their efforts to involve youth, using the news sites and videos, and share what they gathered.

2.t: Video and reflection: Sharing the story found and reflecting on it
2.y: Groups share what they found in a recorded presentation and write an individual reflection in class on the project.

2.t: Yesterday, today, tomorrow: Tracing what came before a pictured object
2.y: Students are given a picture of a floppy disk and a puzzle about what existed before such objects and what comes next; the later search and drawing pursue it.

1.t: Friendship: Noting what they learnt and what more they want to learn
1.y: After each lesson or the unit, students record what they learnt and what else they want to learn in the textbook's reflection section.

2.t: Newspaper article: Drafting, peer editing and reflecting
2.y: Groups draft the article, peer-edit it and revise before submission, then each writes an individual reflection on the work.

3.t: Youth and society: Saying what community work they would like to do
3.y: Students share a news report showing care for the community, then discuss what such care means and what community service they themselves want to do.

2.t: Newspaper article: Choosing an interviewee and making an own product
2.y: Groups choose their own interviewee from the school community and make a newspaper article and video that they own.

1.t: Friendship: Telling a chosen friend a quality they like in them
1.y: Students name friends, pick one and tell them a quality they like, then talk about how they met and what they appreciate; this appreciating task is short.

terms.1: The arts · Me and my relationships · Leadership qualities · WA1
terms.2: Living in harmony with nature · The Tamil way of life · WA2 · Oral
terms.3: Mental well-being · Tamil and the world · AA

1.t: The arts: Giving a view on how Singapore values Tamil traditional arts
1.y: Students read a news report on street theatre in Singapore before class, then comment on the place given to Tamil arts here. A single issue; no tension of views is set.

1.t: Me and my relationships: Why unity matters in a multiracial Singapore
1.y: After a listening task on a story about Singapore children, students discuss why people of many races here need to stay united. Partial at this level: discussion only.

3.t: Mental well-being: Interviewing a parent, student and officer on student mental health
3.y: After news reports on Singapore's efforts, groups act as parent, student, government officer and reporter, swapping roles, so several sides are voiced. Role-play, not debate.

3.t: Debate: Arguing for or against a set question on culture in Singapore
3.y: Students argue for or against a set question on culture in Singapore, with both sides heard. Partial at Level 4: the tension is aired, not worked through.

1.t: Me and my relationships: Saying what they would do in a character's place
1.y: After reading a family dialogue, each student writes on the learning platform what they would do in the character's position. Taking a position in writing, not a live reply.

3.t: Mental well-being: Answering in role as a parent, student or officer
3.y: In a three-step interview each student takes on another person's position on student mental health and answers a reporter, then roles swap.

3.t: Mental well-being: Hot seat as story characters, voicing their feelings
3.y: A student sits in role as a story character and speaks of joy, regret or anger over their actions while classmates question them, with each key character in turn.

1.t: Leadership qualities: How everyday speech differs from speaking on a stage
1.y: Before writing a speech, students discuss what is alike and different between ordinary talk and stage speaking, which shapes how they then write theirs.

3.t: Tamil and the world: Comparing radio programmes with podcasts
3.y: Students listen to a Singapore radio programme, discuss Tamil broadcasts abroad, and talk about what is alike and different between radio and podcasts. Discussion only.

2.t: Oral exam: Answering examiner questions on a video
2.y: After a short video, students answer examiner questions: their reaction or experience, what they suggest, and whether they agree with a given view, giving reasons. Spoken, with the examiner.

4.t: Email: Replying to a friend, or writing in a role to a stated reader
4.y: Students choose one email task: reply to a friend's email, or write in an imagined role to a stated reader for a set purpose. One-way writing for a set purpose and reader.

3.t: Debate speech: Arguing a position with reasons and evidence
3.y: Students prepare and deliver a debate speech of about 2 to 3 minutes with reasons and evidence, and rebut the other side. Spoken to a class audience.

3.t: Mental well-being: Making encouraging e-stickers and judging which slogan is best
3.y: Students design e-sticker slogans for a given situation, show them, and groups discuss which is best and why before the class picks one.

1.t: The arts: Recording podcast episodes on art works and friends' creations, with notes
1.y: Students prepare short notes and record a series of podcast episodes, including talking about a friend's art work, then add a closing summary and upload. One way, aimed at listeners.

1.t: Me and my relationships: Debating a set motion with peer comments
1.y: Students learn debating skills from a video, prepare points and debate a set motion in groups, then classmates comment. The aim is persuading an audience.

1.t: Leadership qualities: Writing and giving a short speech, with classmates' comments
1.y: Students study sample speeches, write a short speech on a set topic and deliver or record it; classmates give comments. The audience and purpose are set.

1.t: Leadership qualities: Group choosing its leader and ranking leadership qualities
1.y: Groups discuss ten leadership qualities, decide among themselves who leads and which qualities matter most, and explain to the class why theirs outrank others. No conflict handling is described.

1.t: Me and my relationships: Raising their own questions on family-relation words
1.y: Faced with relationship words, pairs say which are new, what questions arise for them and which they want to learn more about, before going on.

3.t: Mental well-being: Noting what they know and want to know about gardening for wellbeing
3.y: Before reading, students type what they already know and what they want to know about gardening for mental health; the teacher reads their questions first.

1.t: The arts: Finding out about Singapore's well-known buildings
1.y: An optional add-on to the architecture reading: students find out about famous buildings in Singapore and what makes them special, then share in class.

2.t: The Tamil way of life: Finding stories of people who rose from poverty
2.y: After reading a life story, students use their devices to search for similar stories of people who overcame poverty and share them in class.

2.t: Living in harmony with nature: Gathering facts on nature lovers and spots in Singapore
2.y: Students collect information on nature enthusiasts and on natural places in Singapore before class and share what they found with the class.

3.t: Mental well-being: Discussing why gratitude matters, then thanking a charity by email
3.y: Students discuss why thanks matter and what it brings, pool in groups what to bear in mind when thanking someone, then write a formal thank-you email to a charity.

1.t: Me and my relationships: Naming feelings in family situations and rating how they felt
1.y: Students pick a feeling and situation from the wheels, tell an incident, and show with a finger poll how they felt after the activity, giving reasons.

1.t: The arts: Sharing own dance, music or drawings with the class
1.y: Students who learn dance, music or drawing prepare to show their own work or a recording, upload it, and classmates view it and respond with their views.

1.t: Me and my relationships: Turning a negative family situation into a positive one
1.y: Students spin wheels for a relationship, situation and feeling, share a real or imagined incident, and classmates help the sharer turn a negative situation positive.

2.t: Living in harmony with nature: Recording a commentary, self-assessing, getting feedback
2.y: Students give a live commentary on a nature scene, upload it, assess themselves against stated criteria and then receive written teacher feedback.

3.t: Mental well-being: Discussing how tending plants affects feelings and mental health
3.y: Students bring photos of plants they grow, talk about feelings when tending plants and how that supports mental health, then make a brochure on gardening for mental well-being.

terms.1: Rights and duties · Traditions and customs · Nation-building · NWA1 · Oral
terms.2: Entrepreneurship · Creation and progress · A brand-new Earth · Timed practice
terms.3: SEC oral · Prelim · Revision

1.t: Traditions and customs: Debating whether school events help students learn heritage
1.y: After news on heritage activities in Singapore, students say why they matter, then argue two sides on whether school events help. Sides are set; the teacher judges.

1.t: Nation-building: Jigsaw on Singapore then, now and why it grew
1.y: Expert groups use their own devices to find out about Singapore past and present and the reasons for its growth, then teach mixed groups. One account, not rival views. Guide tagged.

1.t: Nation-building: Working from their own questions on racial harmony
1.y: Before reading on living united across differences, students note three words and two questions on the title, then read and discuss. Guide tagged; one reading, single line.

2.t: Entrepreneurship: News on support for women entrepreneurs and strains on old trades
2.y: From a news report students think about support for women entrepreneurs in Singapore, and the problems and fixes of family trades. Partial: no tension of views.

2.t: A brand-new Earth: Finding out member countries' roles in ASEAN and its benefits
2.y: Students find out before class what ASEAN countries do, discuss the reading in groups and the gains of its work, and share. Guide tagged; regional, with Singapore implicit.

1.t: Traditions and customs: Arguing a side in a class debate on school heritage events
1.y: Two sides put a case on whether school heritage events work, and the teacher names the stronger group and suggests how others can improve.

1.t: Oral exam: Answering examiner questions on a video in SEC format
1.y: After viewing a video, students take part in a discussion with examiners about the video theme, giving experiences, views and reasons. Spoken, with the examiner.

2.t: Entrepreneurship: Two-sided debate on online business
2.y: Two groups recall debate skills from Sec 3 and argue the gains and harms of online business; the teacher judges and praises the groups that argued best.

2.t: Email reply: Replying to a friend's email or writing in a role for set purposes
2.y: Students choose one email task: reply to a friend's email, or write in an imagined role to a stated reader. One-way writing for a set purpose and reader.

1.t: Nation-building: Viewing pictures of Singapore then and now and giving views
1.y: Students give and discuss their views on then-and-now pictures of Singapore, linked to the jigsaw on why it changed. Partial: no new insight is required.

1.t: Nation-building: Group deciding its own video topic, then seeking advice
1.y: Groups discuss and settle what their video will be about, take the teacher's advice, write a short story and record it. Agreement is reached; no conflict handling is set.

2.t: Creation and progress: Fishbowl on questions with no single answer about AI
2.y: An inner circle talks while the rest listen; outer students with differing views swap in and raise them. Partial at this level: no consensus is required.

2.t: Entrepreneurship: Discussing problems and fixes when starting a business
2.y: With teacher guidance, students discuss problems at the start of a business and solutions, and whether new strategies are needed, then type and present their ideas. Partial.

2.t: Entrepreneurship: Think, Puzzle, Explore on family-run trades from the news
2.y: Using the tool, students think about given issues, name problems family trades face, and find out how they tackle them. Prompts are set rather than the students' own.

2.t: A brand-new Earth: Finding what world bodies plan against environmental harm
2.y: Students use their own devices to find out what world bodies plan to fix environmental problems, then discuss it in class.

1.t: Traditions and customs: Interviewing a family member or another person and presenting it
1.y: After studying interview videos and ways to prepare, students interview a family member or someone else and present the interview to the class.

1.t: Nation-building: Jigsaw research on Singapore then and now and reasons for growth
1.y: Using their own devices, expert groups look up Singapore in the past, today or the reasons for its growth, then teach mixed groups.

1.t: Traditions and customs: Sharing interview problems, then writing the experience up
1.y: Students tell the class about their interview and the difficulties they met, then write up the experience in an email.

1.t: Nation-building: Reporting newly learnt facts back to the original group
1.y: After teaching the mixed groups, students return to their first group and share the new information they picked up.

1.t: Nation-building: Listing three words and two questions on racial harmony before reading
1.y: Before reading on racial harmony, students list three words and two questions that the title brings to mind on a worksheet; the teacher notes their thinking.

2.t: A brand-new Earth: Starting from a video of melting glaciers and the causes of harm
2.y: Students watch glaciers melting, discuss causes of environmental harm and describe the new Earth they want; later work looks for solutions.

1.t: Rights and duties: Thanking the last speaker and building on what they said
1.y: In a class round, each student thanks the previous speaker, repeats what they said about rights and duties, then adds a new one. Practises listening.

1.t: Nation-building: Choosing a topic and recording their own group video
1.y: Groups choose what they want to film, write a short story for it and record it, so the topic and product are theirs.

1.t: Traditions and customs: Rewriting an email about their interview after teacher comments
1.y: Students write up their interview experience in parts, get the teacher's comments, rewrite the email to fit them and hand it in again.

1.t: Nation-building: Writing about video-recording challenges and how they were handled
1.y: After recording a group video, students share the problems they met and how they handled them, then write an experience essay on this.

terms.1: New beginnings · Harvest festival · Tamil and me · WA1
terms.2: Life skills · Keeping healthy · WA2 · Oral
terms.3: The internet · Water management · AA

1.t: Harvest festival: Comparing a brochure and a banner on a Venn diagram
1.y: Students write the similarities and differences of the two formats, then make their own banner for its set purpose. Formats rather than cultures are compared.

1.t: New beginnings: Saying what they would do when parents cannot be reached
1.y: In think-pair-share, students say what they would do if they needed something while parents were out, and whether they would talk their decisions over. The guide tags responsible decision-making.

1.t: New beginnings: Advising a friend on a CCA that suits her needs
1.y: Students match CCA details to a friend's stated wishes, choose one and complete a text message advising her. Weaker students fill gaps; abler students write their own.

3.t: Water management: Saying how they would green their school and neighbourhood
3.y: After a news item on planting, students say how they would help keep or make their school and neighbourhood green, given the chance. A short discussion, not a worked plan.

1.t: Tamil and me: Role-playing a dialogue using respectful forms of address
1.y: Students act out a dialogue in spoken Tamil, then note the respectful words used and why the culture expects them. A scripted role-play, so partial.

3.t: Water management: Agreeing or disagreeing with reasons in a round-robin discussion
3.y: Students learn stems for accepting or disputing a view with a reason, then use them in a round-robin talk about water, assessed against a teacher form.

1.t: Harvest festival: Groups summing up members' views on three Pongal questions
1.y: Groups of four, then six, share views on Pongal in Singapore and how to keep festivals alive, sum them up as a group and report to the class.

3.t: The internet: Group talk where members support, dispute or add to ideas
3.y: Using talking chips on whether technology helps us, each member adds a view, explains further, offers an idea, or supports or disputes a groupmate's idea. No group product is set.

1.t: Tamil and me: Talking about where Tamil is used in Singapore
1.y: Students discuss the use of Tamil in Singapore, watch a video on it, and interview a partner about what they saw, including its place in media and public signs.

1.t: Tamil and me: Whether retirees and older Singaporeans need new skills
1.y: With news on SkillsFuture, students discuss whether retirees and older people need to learn new skills, why, and which they would recommend.

1.t: Harvest festival: Discussing how Pongal is kept in Singapore and how to preserve it
1.y: In groups of four then six, students share views on how Pongal is celebrated in Singapore and what to do to keep cultural festivals alive. Views are pooled; no formal contrast of perspectives.

2.t: Keeping healthy: Why healthy living is stressed so often in Singapore
2.y: After a Health Promotion Board video on neighbourhood exercise, students discuss why Singapore keeps stressing a healthy lifestyle. One perspective, so partial.

3.t: Water management: Discussing greening efforts in Singapore from news
3.y: Students share what they know of Singapore's greening efforts and discuss selected news reports on them and the benefits of planting trees. One perspective, so partial.

3.t: Water management: Role-play interview of a minister about Singapore water supply
3.y: Students read about the four national taps and act as reporter and minister to explain how Singapore secures water. Two roles only; one issue.

2.t: Oral exam: Answering examiner questions on a video
2.y: After a short video, students answer examiner questions: their reaction or experience, what they suggest, and what they would do, giving reasons. Spoken, with the examiner.

2.t: Life skills: Planning a short speech on the qualities they want to build
2.y: Students choose one or two qualities from their pledge and plan a short speech for a given situation. One way, as a planned talk.

2.t: Keeping healthy: Writing a reply to a relative email
2.y: Students write a reply to a relative email in the right format and tone for the sender. One way writing, no feedback loop in the task.

4.t: Social media comment: Responding to a post with own experience
4.y: Students take on a named role and write a comment replying to a post, sharing their own experience and feelings in the set number of words. One-way writing for a stated reader.

3.t: Slide presentation: Giving reasons, an experience and benefits on a set topic
3.y: Students prepare 3 to 4 slides and notes on a set topic, giving reasons, an experience and benefits, and present to the class. One-way presentation.

3.t: The internet: Designing and explaining a digital advert for a grocery shop
3.y: Students plan key details, make an advert to attract customers, and explain to the class why they chose its title, pictures and colours.

1.t: Harvest festival: Making a digital banner for the Pongal arts events
1.y: Students gather event details to make an e-banner, show it in a gallery walk where peers rate it, then record an announcement. Mostly one way, with peer feedback on the banner.

3.t: The internet: Jigsaw search for examples of what the internet offers
3.y: Students list daily activities, then in expert groups search online for examples of internet benefits, stressing reliable sources, and report back to their home group.

1.t: Tamil and me: Creating a humorous meme in a group from own experience
1.y: Groups read characters' feelings from a picture, relate them to their own experience and create a humorous meme of their own, with an optional acted version.

1.t: New beginnings: Sharing a first-day story and giving classmates a 3-2-1 response
1.y: Students tell group mates about their first day at secondary school; listeners name three things they liked, ask two questions and name one quality they admire in the speaker.

2.t: Life skills: Three-step interview on the qualities needed to get ahead
2.y: In pairs, one student interviews the other about qualities for success and the interviewer asks why and how follow-ups; pairs then share the quality both like.

3.t: The internet: Talking chips group discussion with listening rules
3.y: Groups use talking chips so only the chip holder speaks while others listen, then add to, support, challenge or ask about an idea.

1.t: New beginnings: Matching their first-day mood to an emotion symbol and describing it
1.y: Students pick the emotion symbol that fits how they felt on the first day of school and describe the experience behind it to their group.

1.t: New beginnings: Reflect-Learn-Act form on what to improve and how
1.y: At the end of the unit students reflect on their participation, list what they learnt and still need help with, and write what they will do to improve.

1.t: Harvest festival: Success, challenge and learning cards at the end of the unit
1.y: In groups of three, students use the feedback they received and picture cards for success, challenge and learnt to reflect on their own progress.

1.t: Tamil and me: Pledge to keep learning Tamil, with a 3-2-1 skills review
1.y: Students complete a pledge on continuing to learn Tamil and its culture, then name three skills learnt, two to improve and one done best.

2.t: Life skills: Listing key life skills and writing a pledge on qualities to build
2.y: Groups discuss five life skills they need, each student completes a pledge on qualities to develop, and groups share their pledges.

2.t: Life skills: 3-2-1 reflection on skills learnt, challenges and one skill to improve
2.y: Students write three skills learnt, two challenging activities and one skill they want to improve, then share with the class.

3.t: Water management: Flower and thorn mindful reflection on what they learnt
3.y: Students use traffic-light cards and a flower and thorn form to record what they learnt and what confused them, then use it to plan their next step.

2.t: Keeping healthy: Guess the Fib on their own healthy habits
2.y: Students write two true habits they follow to stay healthy and one false one, then share with friends who guess the false one.

terms.1: Friendship · Hobbies · Protecting the environment · WA1
terms.2: Cultural norms and values · Yesterday, today, tomorrow · AA · Oral
terms.3: Financial literacy · Youth and society · WA3

2.t: Cultural norms and values: Comparing a circular with adverts, brochures and posters
2.y: Students compare the formats' structure, purpose and layout, say what is alike and different, then write a circular to suit a given situation. Formats rather than cultures are compared.

2.t: Cultural norms and values: Weighing what they would consider in war if they were king
2.y: Groups write answers to questions such as what they would weigh as a king at war and whether all citizens should fight, applying the text to a situation of their own. Discussion only.

3.t: Financial literacy: Deciding between a need and a want and giving reasons
3.y: After a comic on spending, students think through the questions, tell peers the decision they made and explain why, and peers respond. The guide sets needs against wants.

3.t: Financial literacy: Finding ways to spend less at festival time
3.y: With a news report on cutting costs, students say which festive spending is unneeded and why, find ways to be thrifty, and post their views for colour-coded feedback.

1.t: Friendship: Saying what they would do after a quarrel with a friend
1.y: Students discuss what a good friend is like and how they would act when a friendship hits a quarrel. A short lead-in discussion, so partial.

1.t: Hobbies: Judging replies to an online video and imagining the poster view
1.y: Using Step Inside, students imagine the uploader's thinking, then judge whether sample online replies are respectful and rewrite them following courtesy norms.

3.t: Youth and society: Recorded replies to a classmate view on technology and challenges
3.y: Students record a view on a news item, then classmates listen and record a reply to it. Replies are by voice post, not a live exchange.

1.t: Friendship: Summing up two classmates' reasons before adding their own
1.y: In threes, students pass a form and give reasons for friendship qualities; the third sums up the other two and adds a view. Other groups then comment.

1.t: Hobbies: Giving own or differing views after a pair answers in the circle
1.y: In a Spokes circle, a pair answers on hobbies and peers respond with their own or alternative views, keeping to set norms for discussion. A whole-class exchange, with no group decision.

2.t: Cultural norms and values: Brainwriting in threes and sharing the group's ideas
2.y: Each member writes views, passes the sheet to add to others' ideas, and the group shares the combined set with the class.

2.t: Newspaper article: Group drafting and peer editing
2.y: Groups peer-edit the article together and share a single video presentation, taking in each other's suggestions to finish a common product. Evidence of disagreement handling is limited.

1.t: Friendship: Why unity matters in a multiracial society
1.y: In an X-box group discussion, students say why International Friendship Day matters, what they have done with other races, and why a multiracial society needs unity.

1.t: Protecting the environment: Finding out Singapore's green events
1.y: Students visit given sites to find out where Singapore's environmental events happen, who runs them and who takes part, then tell the class. Facts more than perspectives, so partial.

2.t: Cultural norms and values: Singapore's defence today beside ancient forts
2.y: After reading about forts, groups discuss why a country needs defences and what Singapore does for its security today. The guide adds no contrasting view, so partial.

3.t: Financial literacy: Singapore's banknotes, history and a cashless future
3.y: Students discuss changes in Singapore's notes, how their design links to national history, and whether a cashless society may come. The guide tags civic literacy for this unit.

1.t: Social media comment: Responding to a post with own experience

2.t: Oral exam: Answering examiner questions on a video

2.t: Newspaper article and video: Telling a school community member's story

1.t: Protecting the environment: Finding out details of green events online
1.y: Before a class share, students use given links to find where, by whom and for whom events run in Singapore, then report. Teacher-set questions, so structured.

2.t: Interview: Finding out a school community member's story first-hand
2.y: Students interview a real person live in Tamil, ask their own questions and make sense of the replies to build the article. They find out first-hand.

2.t: Video and reflection: Sharing the story found and reflecting on it
2.y: Groups share what they found in a recorded presentation and write an individual reflection in class on the project.

1.t: Protecting the environment: Think, Puzzle, Explore on trees and rain
1.y: Students say what they know about trees, pose their own questions about trees and the environment, and suggest how they could find out more.

2.t: Yesterday, today, tomorrow: Know and want-to-know chart on a new world
2.y: Students write what they already know and what they want to know about a future world, link it to news they read, and share predictions on technology.

3.t: Youth and society: Linking their own service to how youth can contribute
3.y: Through think-pair-share, students share their own community service experience, then discuss what qualities youth need and how they can contribute to society.

3.t: Youth and society: Naming how it feels to serve others
3.y: Students describe a community service they took part in and say what they felt while doing it. A short discussion within a reading lesson.

2.t: Newspaper article: Choosing an interviewee and making an own product
2.y: Groups choose their own interviewee from the school community and make a newspaper article and video that they own.

1.t: Hobbies: Sharing a hobby they do or an old Tamil game that caught their eye
1.y: Each student picks either their own hobby or a traditional Tamil game they find appealing and talks about it confidently to the class.

2.t: Newspaper article: Drafting, peer editing and reflecting
2.y: Groups draft the article, peer-edit it and revise before submission, then each writes an individual reflection on the work.

1.t: Friendship: Pass-the-form discussion on what makes a good friend
1.y: Three students in turn pick friendship qualities with reasons on one form; the third summarises the first two reasons before adding their own.

1.t: The arts: Comparing silambam and silat on a Venn diagram
1.y: After clips of the two martial arts, students note similarities and differences and check them against the textbook notes. Below the Level 4 wording, as no new insight is drawn.

1.t: Leadership qualities: Comparing the duties of different student leaders
1.y: Each student reads about one student leader and shares it, then they compare leaders' responsibilities and tasks on a form. Partial at Level 4.

2.t: The Tamil way of life: Comparing a traditional Tamil house with their Singapore home
2.y: After a video, students name the parts of the old house and of their own home and discuss what is alike and different, then the values each part built. Partial at Level 4.

2.t: The Tamil way of life: Role on the Wall on a poet's and a king's feelings
2.y: Groups write what a poet thinks and feels and how his wife or the king would see him, taking each person's position on a figure on the wall. About text characters, so partial.

1.t: Me and my relationships: Voicing a character's thoughts at key moments in a family scene
1.y: Using thought tracking, students speak aloud how a character feels at turning points, such as a teen torn between friends and a parent call. Perspective-taking; replies are not live.

1.t: The arts: Each member sets questions and leads the group's discussion
1.y: Group members split a text, each prepares discussion questions on their part, asks the others and leads in turn. Shared leading, but Level 4 consensus is not tested.

3.t: Mental well-being: Teams pool evidence and write notes for a class debate
3.y: Students collect evidence on the set topic, write debate notes with their team and argue the case on a class debate stage. Disagreement is across teams, not mediated within them.

1.t: Me and my relationships: Seniors' challenges in a going-digital Singapore
1.y: Students read a news report on the challenges older people face as society goes digital, discuss it and post a recorded response. One news view, so partial at Level 4.

2.t: Living in harmony with nature: Singapore's efforts on food supply
2.y: With news on fish stocks and local farming, students share what they know of government efforts against food shortage and of agriculture in Singapore. Partial at Level 4.

3.t: Debate: Arguing for or against a set question on culture in Singapore
3.y: Students argue for or against a set question on culture in Singapore, with both sides heard. Partial at Level 4: the tension is aired, not worked through.

3.t: Tamil and the world: Collecting classmates' views on Tamil use in Singapore
3.y: Students collect views on Tamil use in Singapore, post voice notes and listen to peers. Views come from classmates; no sharper contrast is set.

2.t: Social media comment: Responding to a post with own experience
2.y: Students take on a named role and write a comment replying to a post, sharing their own experience and feelings in the set number of words. One-way writing for a stated reader.

2.t: Oral exam: Answering examiner questions on a video
2.y: After a short video, students answer examiner questions: their reaction or experience, what they suggest, and whether they agree with a given view, giving reasons. Spoken, with the examiner.

2.t: Living in harmony with nature: Posting a short video or audio response to a news item
2.y: Students record a one to two minute response on a Singapore nature estate news item and peers rate it with a speaking rubric. One way post with peer feedback.

3.t: Debate speech: Arguing a position with reasons and evidence
3.y: Students prepare and deliver a debate speech of about 2 to 3 minutes with reasons and evidence, and rebut the other side. Spoken to a class audience.

3.t: Mental well-being: Tug of War and class debate on whether youth are resilient
3.y: Students take a yes or no stand with written reasons, prepare evidence in teams, argue it, and the other team asks questions or rebuts.

1.t: The arts: Planning and recording a podcast, with peer ratings on a rubric
1.y: Students structure points as topic, reason, example, experience and suggestion for listeners, record, and peers rate recordings against criteria. Persuasive impact is not tested beyond the rubric.

1.t: Leadership qualities: Making a campaign poster for a chosen cause
1.y: Students brainstorm the content, find images online and plan on a form, then make a campaign poster to persuade readers. One way.

2.t: Living in harmony with nature: Know, want to know, learned on farming news
2.y: Students think through a current news item using what they know, what they need to know and what they learned, before a reading on farming in Singapore.

1.t: The arts: Collecting facts on martial arts and comparing them on a Venn diagram
1.y: Students watch clips on silambam and silat, compare them on a Venn diagram and are asked to gather more facts online for a recorded introduction. Guide uses may, so optional.

3.t: Mental well-being: Gathering evidence and points for a class debate
3.y: Students gather evidence and ideas on a debate topic before arguing. A task to support a side, not an open question.

2.t: Living in harmony with nature: How a text prompts them to contribute in future
2.y: Students fill a connections form on places for nature in Singapore, noting whether each idea shifts their view and how it spurs them to contribute later.

3.t: Tamil and the world: Naming a job they want and the skills it needs
3.y: Before an infographic on a job fair, students share what work they want after studying, the qualifications and skills it needs, and link the text to themselves.

1.t: Me and my relationships: Finding and correcting repeated errors in their own writing
1.y: Students pick out sentences with one kind of error from their own work, list them and relearn the rule to fix their drafts.

1.t: The arts: Podcast on a folk art they choose
1.y: Students choose a folk art they like, plan a podcast with a form and combine their recordings for sharing, so the topic and product are their own.

1.t: Me and my relationships: Brainstorming and writing a thank-you note
1.y: Students brainstorm and write a short note of thanks for a given situation and post it on a shared board for others to read.

3.t: Mental well-being: Naming feelings about losing something and ways to cope
3.y: Students discuss which lost item would hurt most, name the feelings tied to loss and share ways of coping, while respecting classmates' feelings.

3.t: Mental well-being: Using the five senses to settle stress and sharing their experience
3.y: Students try a five-senses activity to calm worry or low mood, then share what worked for them.

3.t: Mental well-being: Checking whether their day has time for exercise, rest and family
3.y: Students describe how they spend a day and say whether they set aside time for exercise, hobbies, family and sleep.

1.t: Traditions and customs: How interview questions change with the person interviewed
1.y: Groups discuss how questions differed for a speaker and for students in a news clip, then write interview questions for a news item and may act it out. Partial at Level 4.

1.t: Nation-building: Singapore's transport and National Service, then and now
1.y: Students discuss both services past and present, why they began and how they improved. The guide prints this comparison goal; it stays a discussion, so partial at Level 4.

2.t: Entrepreneurship: Comparing two entrepreneurs in threes
2.y: Groups of three discuss what is alike and different between two entrepreneurs in a text and report to the class. New insight is left to the teacher, so partial at Level 4.

1.t: Nation-building: Travel brochure on a Singapore attraction, revised after peer review
1.y: Students write brochure content for a set situation, a partner comments on the sentences, and they improve it and type it up. One way, with a peer review step.

1.t: Oral exam: Answering examiner questions on a video in SEC format
1.y: After viewing a video, students take part in a discussion with examiners: sharing an experience, suggesting ways forward, and giving a view with reasons. Spoken, with the examiner.

1.t: Rights and duties: Role-playing a job interview and writing preparation notes
1.y: In pairs, one student interviews and one answers appropriately; they then write notes on preparing for an interview, and peers comment. Practice for a set purpose.

1.t: Traditions and customs: Writing questions and role-playing an interview
1.y: Students write reporter questions from a news item on a food festival, role-play the interview, and get teacher comments on question structure.

2.t: Entrepreneurship: Writing a CV and a covering email to an employer
2.y: Students fill in a CV form with their details and learn to attach it to an official email. One way writing for an employer.

2.t: Creation and progress: Critiquing a model advert, then making and improving their own
2.y: Pairs suggest how to improve a model advert and explain why; students then post their own advert, get peer comments and revise it.

2.t: Entrepreneurship: Reporting a group's shared and differing views
2.y: In Think-Talk-Open Exchange-Share on news about student entrepreneurs, members look for common ground and a chosen speaker reports both shared and differing views. No decision is required.

1.t: Nation-building: Why Singapore's public services and National Service began
1.y: Students discuss why these services were started and how they have improved, linking to prior knowledge before a reading. The guide prints CGC 1 for this unit; one account, so partial.

1.t: Traditions and customs: Know, want to know and learned chart on millets
1.y: Students state what they know and want to know about millets, watch a video and judge whether its title fits, before searching further.

1.t: Rights and duties: Know and want-to-know chart on rights and duties
1.y: Students state what they know and what they want to know about rights and duties before the unit.

1.t: Nation-building: Know and want-to-know chart on Singapore's journey
1.y: Students note what they know and want to know about the reading title and link it to news before reading.

2.t: Entrepreneurship: Think, Puzzle, Explore on turning hobbies into small businesses
2.y: Students share what they know, raise their own doubts such as whether every hobby can become a business, and say how to settle them.

1.t: Traditions and customs: Groups search online on a chosen millet and share findings
1.y: Each group searches for facts on one millet from the textbook and a member reports them to classmates, followed by a summary of what they learnt.

1.t: Traditions and customs: Searching online for examples of Tamil dress
1.y: Pairs search online for examples of Tamil traditional dress, choose images, merge into fours to discuss and share findings.

1.t: Traditions and customs: Why a mother is shocked by her children's clothes
1.y: A scene shows a mother shocked at her children's clothes, and students judge whether the clothes are traditional, which leads into a search.

2.t: Entrepreneurship: Planning a small business from a hobby they love
2.y: Students choose a hobby of their own and plan it as a small business in the I am an entrepreneur task.

2.t: Entrepreneurship: Think-Talk-Open Exchange-Share with silent listening
2.y: Students think alone, then in groups one speaks while others only listen, then compare common and different ideas and share the group view.

2.t: Creation and progress: Improving an advert from peer feedback
2.y: Students post their advert, read peer comments, and improve the advert in light of those comments.

1.t: Unit 2: Comparing how places around the world mark the New Year

2.t: Unit 3: Comparing tourist route maps
2.y: Groups compare two local route maps on sites chosen, theme, audience and presentation, then say which they prefer. Optional extension.

3.t: Unit 5: Comparing two competition posters
3.y: Students find a second competition poster online and compare the two, noting similarities and differences. Optional extension.

2.t: Unit 3: Designing a three-day itinerary for a foreign friend
2.y: Groups decide what best shows Singapore, then design an itinerary to suit a foreign friend's wish to know it in depth.

3.t: Unit 5: Weighing views on changing animal genes
3.y: Students take a stance on changing animal genes, are challenged with views for and against, and post and comment on SLS.

3.t: Unit 5: Inventing a product for an everyday problem
3.y: Students work out what is inconvenient in daily life and what product could fix it, then write a plan for its users.

3.t: Unit 6: Role-playing unsung heroes
3.y: Students take the part of four overlooked workers, share their work and feelings, and answer classmates' questions. Optional extension.

2.t: Oral: Imagining being a person in the video
2.y: One oral question asks students to imagine being a person in the video and say how they would feel and why. This is perspective-taking in speech, tested one to one.

2.t: Unit 4: Group talk on how habits affect others, replying to peers
2.y: In threes, each student gives a view on habits and the others respond by agreeing, adding or disagreeing; the class then asks questions of group reporters.

1.t: Unit 2: Discussing whether New Year customs should be kept, answering each view
1.y: In groups, one student gives a view on keeping customs and the others reply by agreeing, adding or disagreeing, then they swap roles.

1.t: Unit 2: Comparing views on reunion dinner as a group
1.y: Groups compare what each member collected, note what is the same or different, sum it up and make a slide deck.

2.t: Unit 3: Groups build an itinerary and give each other feedback
2.y: Groups draw up a shared plan, view other groups' plans in shared files, and exchange feedback and views.

3.t: Unit 5: Groups agree whom to interview and outline it together
3.y: Groups discuss and choose a person to interview, research online, fill in the outline together and check other groups' outlines.

3.t: Unit 5: Agreeing on and presenting a product plan as a group
3.y: Groups settle on one product, complete the plan together and present it, then take other groups' questions.

2.t: Unit 3: Singapore's places, food and cultures
2.y: The CPDD guide names CGC 1.3 as a goal of Unit 3: students get to know Singapore through its places, food and many cultures.

3.t: Unit 6: Local workers' contribution; fact and opinion in the news
3.y: Students examine what local train maintenance staff contribute, how a commuter's view changes, and fact versus opinion in the report.

1.t: Unit 2: Interviewing people on whether CNY means going home for reunion dinner
1.y: Students gather views on a Singapore festival practice from news and interviews and compare differing opinions. Partial: the topic is cultural custom, not a policy issue.

2.t: WA2: Email sharing experience and a view
2.y: Students reply to a friend's email, answering the points raised for a stated purpose. Written exam task, one way only.

2.t: Oral: Experience, reasons and suggestions, and a view on a statement
2.y: In a one-to-one oral after a video, students share experience, give reasons and suggestions, or state a view on a statement. Spoken, with the examiner.

2.t: Unit 3: Planning a three-day itinerary for a foreign friend
2.y: Groups plan a three-day visit to Singapore for a foreign friend using web research, then view each other's plans on shared files and give feedback.

2.t: Unit 3: Replying to an email recommending a place and food to a friend abroad
2.y: Students write a reply email to a friend in France, choosing a Singapore sight and food, using numbers and examples for that reader. One way writing.

3.t: Authentic assessment: Formal mock interview video
3.y: Students record a formal mock interview: opening, self-introduction, chosen questions answered with PEEL and an example each, and a closing. One way only.

3.t: Unit 5: Presenting an invention plan to the class
3.y: Groups present a plan for a product that solves a daily problem and field questions from other groups.

3.t: Unit 6: Debating whether to go back to rescue people, giving and opposing reasons
3.y: Students debate a stance, stating a view with reasons and opposing the other side with reasons.

3.t: Unit 6: Making a tribute video about an unsung hero
3.y: Groups of four make a short video introducing and interviewing a chosen unsung hero and thanking them, for classmates to view.

4.t: End-of-year paper: Email and narrative composition
4.y: Students reply to a friend's email, answering the points raised for a stated purpose. Written exam task, one way only. A narrative follows.

1.t: Unit 1: Suggesting ideas for next year's school orientation after viewing news clips
1.y: After watching two orientation news reports, groups discuss their own school's orientation and write suggestions for next year, then share them. A set purpose, mostly one way to the school.

1.t: Unit 2: News clips raise whether reunion dinner must be at home
1.y: News reports are used to spark the question of whether Lunar New Year requires going home for reunion dinner, which the interviews then pursue.

3.t: Unit 5: Pairs share everyday school annoyances to be solved later
3.y: Pairs share small problems from school life; the guide says the later combined task will work on solving them.

1.t: Unit 2: Interviewing people with a record sheet and comparing group findings
1.y: Students interview people with a record sheet, then group members compare what they each found, noting what is the same or different.

2.t: Unit 3: Exploring word origins and regional variants, then presenting
2.y: Groups explore how given words came into Chinese or differ by region, then present their findings and exchange across groups.

3.t: Unit 6: Interviewing a chosen unsung hero for a video
3.y: Groups choose a local unsung hero, find out about their work and interview them for the video.

1.t: Unit 2: Sharing a group briefing and rating other groups
1.y: Groups summarise the interview findings into a briefing, share it, and groups give each other peer ratings.

3.t: Unit 5: Presenting a product plan and answering other groups' questions
3.y: Groups present their invention plan to the class and other groups ask questions and exchange views.

3.t: Unit 6: Sharing videos, voting and optionally reflecting
3.y: Groups show their videos to the class, classmates vote for favourites and may write a short reflection on what they learned.

3.t: Unit 5: Choosing a person to interview and drafting interview questions
3.y: Groups pick a historical figure, research background online and draft interview questions, then check each other's outlines.

3.t: Unit 5: Asking which daily inconvenience a new product could fix
3.y: Before writing a product plan, students think about inconvenient things in life, what could solve them, its look and function, and who uses it.

1.t: Unit 1: Revising a classmate description after others' guesses
1.y: Groups describe a classmate for others to guess, hear why wrong guessers were misled, note the feedback and revise their description.

2.t: Unit 4: Sticking to a 21-day challenge and reflecting on perseverance
2.y: Students set and keep a long challenge, then reflect and share what it took, linking new habits to perseverance and resolve.

2.t: Unit 4: Talking with a partner about own good and bad habits
2.y: Pairs say what good and bad habits they have, how good ones were built and how bad ones could be dropped.

2.t: Unit 4: A 21-day habit challenge with a daily progress record
2.y: Students keep a 21-day challenge, record each day's progress in a table, and share the process and reflections on a platform.

3.t: Unit 6: Showing respect to an unsung hero through interview and video
3.y: Students interview someone who serves them and express respect in a tribute video, practising appreciating others.

2.y: Students work out what rites from different places and periods share and how they differ, then consider why such rites matter.

1.t: Unit 1: Deciding how to handle a parent-teen clash
1.y: After debating a clip, students think how to respond to the situation so that the parent-child relationship is not harmed.

3.t: Unit 5: Planning an ideal town as a planner who serves residents
3.y: Students apply the unit's learning in an interactive game, planning a town around people's needs and explaining their choices.

1.t: Unit 1: Role-playing a father or mother to grasp different reactions
1.y: Before writing, students take a parent's role to understand how each person reacts to the same situation.

1.t: Unit 2: Speaking as the wrongly accused cat

1.t: Unit 1: Debating a mother's behaviour in assigned for or against groups

2.t: Unit 4: Handling problems with friends by seeing the other side
2.y: Students share a problem they met with classmates and how they solved it, and are led to think from the other person's side.

3.y: Pairs take turns to respond to another's view by listening, understanding it, then stating agreement or opposition with reasons.

3.t: Unit 5: Groups discuss what future public housing should be like
3.y: Groups discuss and give reasons for what future flats should be like, then share and take questions and challenges.

2.t: Unit 3: Explaining sea-level rise and its effect on Singapore
2.y: Students explain what problem Singapore faces from rising seas, using a chart, and urge classmates to help.

3.t: Unit 5: How public housing and town planning support racial harmony
3.y: Groups discuss what Singapore's flats and town planning do for racial harmony, note points and share them.

3.t: Unit 6: How Singapore stays diverse and open while finding common ground
3.y: Students find where Singapore shows diversity and openness, then discuss how to seek common ground and respect difference.

1.t: Unit 2: Designing a wildlife awareness booklet for the public

2.t: Unit 3: Making a video or poster to encourage saving water and power
2.y: Groups make a short video or poster giving saving tips to persuade others, share it, and classmates vote for favourites.

2.t: Unit 3: Reporting on rising sea levels to classmates to encourage action
2.y: Students give a talk using a chart and animation to explain sea level rise and its effect on Singapore, aimed at encouraging classmates to help.

3.y: Students make a map and recorded script for an ideal town and explain their choices of facilities to classmates.

3.y: Groups present their findings as a poster or briefing; other groups ask questions and exchange views.

1.y: After reading about five ways of feeling loved, students guess how their family members prefer to be shown care, before asking them.

1.t: Unit 1: Asking family how they feel loved and comparing with own guess

3.y: Groups pick an item at home and use labels, manuals and the web to find where materials come from, where made and where sold.

1.t: Unit 1: Sharing family reactions after showing care
1.y: After trying to show care in their family member's preferred way, students share the family's reactions online.

1.t: Unit 2: Presenting the booklet and answering other groups' questions
1.y: Groups share their booklet with the class, other groups ask questions and exchange views, and the booklets are displayed.

3.t: Unit 5: Sharing ideal town maps and critiquing each other's choices
3.y: Students present their town map and the reasons for chosen facilities, and classmates respond on what they liked and would improve.

3.t: Unit 6: Presenting item journeys and sharing what they realised
3.y: Groups present a poster or briefing, take questions, and talk about what they found or realised about global links.

3.t: Unit 5: Asking what an ideal town should be like
3.y: After the unit, students think about what an ideal town is like, taking a town planner's view before designing.

1.t: Unit 1: Showing care to family in the way each person feels loved
1.y: Students plan and try an action to show care to a family member, based on what that person said makes them feel loved.

1.t: Unit 2: Making a booklet that helps the public coexist with wildlife
1.y: Students use research and design skills to make a booklet that educates others, so the public can protect wild animals.

2.y: Students use their own household data and creativity to make a video or poster urging others to conserve.

2.y: Students record a talk on sea level rise, listen to classmates' recordings, give feedback, note what to adjust and record again.

2.y: Students record views on an event, get peer feedback, note changes and record a second time.

3.t: Unit 6: Views on how characters act in different situations
3.y: The CPDD guide names CAIT 3.4 as a goal of Unit 6: students say what they think of how characters act in different situations. Sits in reading.

1.t: Unit 2: Comparing tea-drinking habits across places and races
1.y: Students discuss how tea habits differ between places and among Singapore's races, with examples. Partial: a discussion after reading.

2.t: Unit 3: Comparing free community clinics then and now
2.y: Students say how services have and have not changed, then discuss whether society still needs them.

2.t: Unit 4: Matching ways of communicating to occasions and audiences
2.y: Groups discuss which communication channels suit which occasions and people, and what to watch for in each, then share and question each other.

3.t: Unit 6: Responding with empathy and respect
3.y: The CPDD guide names CCI 2.4 as a goal of Unit 6: students communicate with empathy and respect in reading talk, speaking and the group task.

3.t: Unit 6: Comparing a friend's and the author's views on begging, then forming own view
3.y: Students compare two views on begging, with the guide stressing empathy, then settle and explain their own view. Partial: sits in a reading task.

1.t: Unit 1: Imagining a friend's thoughts on opening a gift jar
1.y: Students imagine themselves as a story's character and say what she would think, then see the kind intent behind an act.

2.t: Unit 4: How to communicate with people of other races and cultures
2.y: Drawing on their own lives, students discuss how to talk with people of other backgrounds, such as learning customs and reading reactions.

2.t: Unit 4: Thinking how online words affect the other person
2.y: Groups discuss how to avoid the harms of social media, including thinking from the other person's side before posting.

1.t: Unit 1: Saying whether they would act as a story's character did
1.y: Students put themselves in the character's place, decide what they would do, and explain it, in groups then to the class.

2.t: Unit 3: Weighing whether joining a community chat group does more good
2.y: Groups weigh the benefits and drawbacks for daily life, then say whether they agree and why.

3.t: Unit 5: Arguing a chosen position using contrast
3.y: Students take a position, argue it using contrast, and classmates with other positions speak, add to it or comment.

2.t: Unit 3: Groups split work and agree on evidence for an argument
2.y: Groups discuss and share out work to find fitting examples and sayings, present them, and classmates judge if they fit.

2.t: Unit 4: How Singapore builds racial harmony
2.y: Students explain how Singapore strengthens racial harmony and name further measures they know. Partial: one view, in a reading task.

2.t: Unit 3: Weighing how well society cares for older people
2.y: Using news on elderly policies and on negative reports, students discuss what is done well and poorly, optionally in groups or a debate. Teacher led and partial.

3.t: Authentic assessment: Analysing at least two views on a community issue
3.y: Groups choose a community issue from a list, analyse at least two different viewpoints and then take a stance.

4.t: End-of-year paper: Forum post on a community issue with differing views
4.y: The forum task presents a community issue with differing netizen views, which students must address before giving their own. Written exam task, one way only.

2.t: WA2: Formal email in a stated role for a stated purpose
2.y: Students write a formal email in a stated role to a stated type of recipient, describing a problem, its effects and proposed improvements. One way only.

2.t: Oral: Planned response with a stance, then follow-up questions
2.y: In a one-to-one oral, students give a planned response with a stance and video evidence, then answer follow-up questions. Spoken, with the examiner.

2.t: Unit 4: Presenting a group chart on suitable communication channels
2.y: Groups present their findings on choosing channels for different audiences and classmates ask questions of each other.

3.t: Authentic assessment: Group news video taking a stance on an issue
3.y: Groups of four record a 5 to 7 minute news-style video taking a stance on an issue, using three argument methods and an interactive spoken style for the audience.

4.t: End-of-year paper: Forum post from several posts, composition
4.y: Students read several forum posts and write their own, stating a view and suggestions and addressing at least two posters. Exam task, one way only. A composition follows.

1.t: Unit 1: Retelling a hair-donation story to encourage family and friends to join
1.y: Students retell an event in order, stressing the points that suit the aim of persuading relatives and friends to take part, and leaving out the rest.

3.t: Authentic assessment: Choosing an issue and a stance
3.y: Groups pick one issue from a list, or propose their own for approval, and fix their stance before researching.

3.t: Unit 5: Choosing an interviewee and preparing an interview record sheet
3.y: Students decide whom to interview and fill in the record sheet, with tips on interviewing, before going out.

2.t: Unit 3: Brainstorming a free-choice task for a community bingo challenge
2.y: Students brainstorm what their own open task could be, which must fit the community theme and not repeat the other tasks.

3.t: Authentic assessment: Gathering reliable evidence and interview content
3.y: Groups collect information, filter reliable arguments and add interview content to the script, as the workflow checklist lists.

3.t: Unit 5: Interviewing someone with five years' experience on how their job changed
3.y: Students interview an experienced worker about changes since they started and their view of the future, noting photos and impressions.

1.t: Unit 2: Tracking own diet, exercise and sleep for a week and analysing it
1.y: Students gather data on their own habits over a week, then analyse and sum up where change is needed.

2.t: Unit 3: Exploring the neighbourhood and recording people, places and feelings
2.y: Students complete community tasks outside class, taking photos and noting interesting people, things and their own feelings.

3.t: Authentic assessment: Presenting the stance as a news video
3.y: Groups record and share a news-style video presenting their analysed stance to an audience.

3.t: Unit 5: Pairs exchange interview records and main takeaways
3.y: Students post interview points, then pair up to exchange records and what they gained, and some share with the class.

1.t: Unit 2: Swapping health diaries in groups and suggesting improvements
1.y: Students exchange diaries with group members, learn about each other's habits, and evaluate them with suggestions.

2.t: Unit 3: Presenting community posts and saying what they newly understood
2.y: Students post their findings, read classmates', some present in class, and say what they feel or now understand about the community.

1.t: Unit 2: News on Singaporeans' exercise habits prompts why they do not exercise more
1.y: A news video on healthy eating but low exercise is used to raise questions on survey findings and why people do not exercise more.

3.t: Unit 5: News on robots and jobs sets up how work changes
3.y: A news video on cleaners and robots prompts students to say how the cleaning job changed and how workers feel, before choosing whom to interview.

1.t: Unit 1: Revising writing from peer review suggestions
1.y: Groups discuss outlines, give peer review, and each student uses the suggestions to improve the draft.

3.t: Unit 5: Self and peer review, then revising an argument
3.y: Students check their argument against a checklist alone and with peers, revise it, then hand it in.

3.t: Authentic assessment: Choosing the issue
3.y: Groups choose an issue from a list of paired statements, or propose their own with approval.

2.t: Unit 3: Setting a free-choice task in a community bingo challenge
2.y: Students make their own task within the theme and create a personal social media post about what they saw and felt.

1.t: Unit 1: Sharing song lyrics that inspire how they handle friendships
1.y: Students choose songs and share how the lyrics guide how they treat others, kept to the angle of managing relationships.

1.t: Unit 1: Optional card to self on weak points in building relationships
1.y: Optional extension: students reflect on where they fall short in building relationships and write themselves a card of reminders for the year.

1.t: Unit 2: Keeping a one-week health diary of eating, exercise and sleep
1.y: Students record a week of diet, exercise and sleep, then reflect on which areas to adjust.

3.t: Unit 6: Capturing truth, goodness and beauty around them with feelings noted
3.y: Students photograph what they notice as true, good or beautiful in daily life and record what they saw and felt, then share in groups.

3.t: Unit 6: Optional thank-you note to someone who showed goodness
3.y: Optional extension: students write a note thanking a person who made them feel truth, goodness or beauty.

3.t: Unit 6: Optional sticky-note pledge of one kind act for the week
3.y: Optional extension: students reflect on how to practise goodness, write one kind act for the week on a note, and remove it when done.
