1.y: Students plan in groups, write a review covering feelings, purpose and problem, and a group presents it; written and one way, aimed at readers who might buy.

1.t: Unit 2: Naming group members' talents and setting roles for a self-expression piece
1.y: Groups choose a medium and theme, identify each member's talent and fix roles; no reflection on how the group worked is set, so only partly meets this level.

2.t: Unit 4: Groups plan a social business to help a group in need
2.y: Groups choose which social business to run or support and complete a planning template; it is a paper plan with others, nothing is carried out in the community.

1.t: Unit 2: Searching news sites for articles on Malay performing arts and youth
1.y: Students look through news sites for further articles on the question and give a written response; the guide marks this as an inquiry learning experience.

1.t: Unit 1: Searching news for articles on the Maintenance of Parents Act
1.y: Students search news sites for more articles on whether elderly parents may claim support, to inform their view; they find the material themselves.

2.t: Unit 3: Searching the internet for what two community figures contributed
2.y: Students search online for more about two role models' achievements and contributions before listing them in pairs.

2.t: Unit 4: Searching for social businesses in Singapore and who they help
2.y: Students look up news on Singapore social businesses and answer who is helped and what business is run.

2.t: Unit 4: Investigating and planning a social business to help people in need
2.y: The guide names this as inquiry-based learning: students investigate and explore how to help a group facing difficulty and plan a social business.

3.t: Unit 5: Searching the web on the 1992 crop circles and sharing in a round robin
3.y: Students look up the Berkshire crop circles themselves and share what they find, leading to the point that phenomena have reasonable explanations.

3.t: Unit 5: Searching news on mystery channels in social media
3.y: Students read news about mystery channels, share the story with classmates and react; the guide labels this an inquiry learning experience.

3.t: Unit 6: Groups find articles on creative ways to secure local food supply
3.y: Each group member picks an article or video, then shares the main message and why it matters, using reciprocal teaching.

3.t: Unit 6: Searching the internet about refugee camps before discussing support
3.y: Students research refugee camps online, then discuss how to support the children before writing their views.

1.t: Unit 2: Posting a response and questioning a partner's response online
1.y: Students post their answer and comment on or ask about another pair's answer, sharing findings with feedback; part of the guide's inquiry learning experience.

2.t: Unit 4: Presenting the business plan, with self-check and peer evaluation
2.y: Groups present the plan and classmates and teacher give feedback; students check their own script and complete a peer evaluation. Follows the unit's named inquiry task.

3.y: After researching, students write a message with their reasons and ways to help, and classmates comment on it online.

2.y: Students retell the main points to family and friends and give their own view to encourage helping people with disabilities join society. One-way spoken task.

1.t: Unit 3: Researching a local dialect group to explain its features
1.y: Students search online for facts on one Chinese dialect group, such as population, food and customs, choose features and explain them with examples and numbers. Department reading.

2.t: Unit 4: Interviewing someone with five years of work experience
2.y: Students choose an interviewee, ask how their job has changed and what they expect ahead, noting their own reactions. Department reading; questions are partly set.

2.t: Unit 5: Observing their neighbourhood for features that include everyone
2.y: Students walk their own community, photograph and note facilities, activities and schemes that help build an inclusive society, then share in groups. Department reading.

2.t: Unit 4: Comparing interview records and main takeaways in pairs
2.y: Students post interview notes online, then swap records in pairs and discuss the main findings before sharing with the class. Department reading.

1.t: Unit 2: Sharing a goal they achieved and what it taught them
1.y: Students recount a time they reached a goal and their reflections, then find and share a well-known person's success story and what it taught them.

1.t: Unit 2: Writing a letter to their future self about hopes, worries and plans
1.y: Students think about the person they want to be, name worries and write how they plan to make that future happen, then share part of the letter.

1.t: Unit 3: Designing their own Made in Singapore product blending two cultures
1.y: Students pick a Chinese food or object, add features from another community, explain the meaning of their design and present it in pairs, with questions from others.

2.t: Unit 5: Suggesting community improvements that would make it more inclusive
2.y: Groups share what they want added or improved in their neighbourhood for inclusion, and one member presents the group's suggestions. Suggestions stay within class.

1.label: Chinese (CL)
1.title: Interview 101: student leader interview
1.format: Recorded interview video, about 3 minutes, with a written draft. Individual.
1.when: Term 3, W2 to W6. Submitted 4 Aug 2026.
1.builds: Builds on Term 2 oral practice: sharing experiences and giving suggestions.

CCI 1.t: Make a PEEL case for the role, with real examples
CCI 1.y: The rubric rewards clear organisation, PEEL and concrete examples. It is framed as a real interview, so purpose and context are clear. One way only: students do not build ideas with others.

CCI 1.t: Show understanding of a student leader’s duties
CCI 1.y: The top band asks for understanding of the duties of a student leader, and the draft asks how students would help teachers and classmates.

1.label: Malay (ML)
1.title: Makanan Kegemaran: my favourite food
1.format: Oral presentation, 2 minutes, with a written script. Individual.
1.builds: Builds on Unit 6: Come and eat (the food unit in the CPDD sample scheme).

CAIT 3.t: Link the dish to its traditional or fusion form
CAIT 3.y: The prompt asks what fusion dish could be created from a traditional one, or which tradition lies behind a fusion dish. No rubric line rewards this.

CCI 1.t: Organise and present the story with 4P
CCI 1.y: Students organise experience, feeling, opinion and lesson into a script, then present to an audience. The rubric rewards well-developed ideas with examples. One way only.

1.label: Tamil (TL)
1.title: The CCA I Like
1.format: Recorded slide presentation, 4–5 slides, 2–3 minutes, uploaded to SLS. Individual.
1.builds: Builds on the “The CCA I like” recording in 1A Module 1 (activity 1.4).

CCI 1.t: Explain a CCA clearly, with examples, on slides
CCI 1.y: The rubric rewards clear, connected ideas with examples, fitting images and engaged delivery. The prompts are descriptive (what, why, benefits, an experience) and one way only.

1.label: Chinese (CL)
1.title: Interview video: talking about my character
1.format: Recorded interview answer of 1 to 2 minutes with a written script of 200 to 250 characters. Individual.
1.builds: Builds on Term 2 oral practice in sharing experiences and giving reasons with examples, and on PEEL.

CCI 1.t: Present two personal traits with PEEL and examples
CCI 1.y: Students organise two traits, each with an example, into a short script and record it as a mock interview answer. One way only: no exchange with the listener.

1.label: Chinese (CL)
1.title: Interview 101: mock overseas immersion interview
1.format: Recorded formal mock interview of 5 to 7 minutes with a written final script; students choose 3 questions. Individual.
1.when: Term 3, submitted 4 Aug 2026 (draft in Term 3 W1 to W2).
1.builds: Builds on Term 2 oral work in giving reasons with examples; teacher introduces the task at the end of Term 2.

CCI 1.t: Answer formally with PEEL and an example for each question
CCI 1.y: Students open, introduce themselves, answer three self-chosen questions with a point, explanation, example and link, then close, all in formal Chinese for an interview panel. One way only.

1.label: Malay (ML)
1.title: WA3 oral presentation about a favourite food
1.format: Individual script and 1.5 to 2.5 minute class presentation on a given theme, scored on script, delivery and content; the Higher Malay version adds spontaneous questions.
1.builds: Sec 1 recount and descriptive speaking, planning with a mind map and using the standard presentation opening and closing.

CCI 1.t: WA3 authentic task: oral presentation about a favourite food, scripted then delivered
CCI 1.y: Students plan a script on a given theme, then present it to the class for a stated length. One way only, with a spoken delivery rubric.

Accomplishment.t: WA3 authentic task: drafting a presentation script, getting feedback, then rehearsing
Accomplishment.y: Students draft a mind map and script, get peer or teacher comments on the script, rehearse, then present against a rubric. Improvement from feedback, not only a one-off task.

1.label: Tamil (TL)
1.title: My favourite CCA: individual slide presentation (G1, G2)
1.format: Solo class presentation of 2 to 3 minutes with 3 to 4 slides and speaker notes on a favourite CCA: which one, why, an introduction to it, and what it gives them.
1.builds: The task sheet names no unit; it supplies sentence frames for giving reasons, an experience and benefits.

CCI 1.t: CCA presentation: Sharing reasons, experience and benefits of a favourite CCA
CCI 1.y: Students prepare 3 to 4 slides and notes on their favourite CCA, giving reasons, an experience and benefits, and present to the class. One-way presentation.

1.label: Tamil (TL)
1.title: My favourite CCA: individual slide presentation with a challenge (HTL)
1.format: Solo class presentation of up to 4 minutes with 4 to 5 slides on a favourite CCA, adding a challenge faced and how it was overcome.
1.builds: The task sheet names no unit; it adds a challenge-and-response prompt to the G1 to G3 version.

CCI 1.t: CCA presentation: Sharing a favourite CCA, its benefits and a challenge
CCI 1.y: Students prepare 4 to 5 slides and notes on a favourite CCA, covering why they like it, benefits and a challenge, and present to the class. One-way presentation.

Accomplishment.t: CCA presentation: Describing a challenge met and how it was overcome
Accomplishment.y: Students describe a challenge met in their CCA and how they overcame it, reflecting on what their own experience taught them.

2.label: Chinese (CL)
2.title: 40 Stories: people of BVSS (interview, news report, video)
2.format: Group project in 4 parts (100 marks): interview recording 5, news report in Chinese 45, group video presentation 45, personal written reflection 5. Groups of 2 to 3 (G2) or 4 to 5 (G3).
2.when: Term 2: nominations Term 1 W10, interviews T2W1 to W2, drafting T2W3 to W5, submission T2W7.
2.builds: Builds on Term 1 learning of interview and reporting skills in class and the Sec 2 emphasis on narrating real experience.

CCI 1.t: Interview a person linked to the school and tell the story
CCI 1.y: Groups convey the interviewee's story for readers in a news report and for an audience in a recorded group video. Interviewees are chosen by the group.

Conceptualisation.t: Choose an interviewee and plan the questions
Conceptualisation.y: Groups nominate whom to interview and write their own questions in addition to the set ones.

Investigation.t: Hold a real interview and submit a recording
Investigation.y: Groups interview in Chinese for about 10 to 20 minutes in person, by video or by phone, and record it as evidence.

Conclusion.t: Report, present and reflect on what was learned
Conclusion.y: Groups write and present the story, and each student reflects in writing on what they learned about the interviewee.

Engagement.y: Groups choose from anyone linked to the school, and strong students are encouraged to approach well-known alumni.

Accomplishment.t: Peer review and revise the news report
Accomplishment.y: Drafting includes peer review and revision before final submission; the mid-way peer review is ungraded.

2.label: Malay (ML)
2.title: WA2 40 Stories of BVSS: interview a person linked to the school
2.format: Group project: recorded interview, newspaper article in the mother tongue, group oral video and an individual in-class reflection, 100 marks in all.
2.builds: Interview skills lessons in Term 2 Weeks 1 to 2, with interviewee nomination from Term 1 Week 10 and Sec 2 article writing.

CCI 1.t: WA2 authentic task: interview a person linked to BVSS, then write an article and present a video
CCI 1.y: Students turn interview findings into a mother tongue newspaper article and a recorded oral presentation for readers and viewers. The article and video are one way, with no audience reply.

CCI 2.t: WA2 authentic task: conducting a live interview in the mother tongue
CCI 2.y: Students interview a real person from the school community, listen actively, ask follow-up questions and adjust their language to suit the interviewee. Respect and empathy are partly shown.

CCI 3.t: WA2 authentic task: group roles, peer editing and a mid-point peer check
CCI 3.y: Groups share roles, peer edit the article draft together, and complete an ungraded mid-point peer rating of each member's contribution. Taking suggestions is stated; managing disagreement is not.

Conceptualisation.t: WA2 authentic task: preparing interview questions from background research
Conceptualisation.y: Before interviewing, groups research the person's background and write their own structured questions. They choose what to find out and plan how.

Investigation.t: WA2 authentic task: carrying out a live interview and recording it
Investigation.y: Students find out first-hand by interviewing a real person for about ten to twenty minutes, record it, and make sense of what they learn for the article.

Conclusion.t: WA2 authentic task: sharing the story, then an individual written reflection
Conclusion.y: Groups share what they found as an article and a video. In class, each student then writes what they learned about the interviewee and from the experience.

Accomplishment.t: WA2 authentic task: peer editing the article draft and reflecting on the project
Accomplishment.y: Students improve an article draft through peer editing against the rubric, then write a personal reflection on what they learned from the experience.

Engagement.t: WA2 authentic task: choosing an interviewee and making a newspaper story
Engagement.y: Students nominate people they want to interview from a pool of the school community, then craft the story of that person as an article and video they own.

2.label: Tamil (TL)
2.title: 40 Stories of BVSS: interview and newspaper article
2.format: Group (2 to 5) interviews a real person linked to BVSS in Tamil, writes a newspaper article on the story, records a group video presentation, and each writes an individual reflection in class. G1 to H differ in group size and word count.
2.when: Term 2, submitted via SLS in Week 7
2.builds: Interview skills lessons in Term 2 Weeks 1 to 2 come before the interview, per the assignment guide.

CCI 1.t: Newspaper article and video: Telling a school community member's story
CCI 1.y: Students interview a real person, then convey the story in a newspaper article and a recorded presentation for readers and viewers. Largely one-way presentation to an audience.

CCI 3.t: Newspaper article: Group drafting and peer editing
CCI 3.y: Groups peer-edit the article together and share a single video presentation, taking in each other's suggestions to finish a common product. Evidence of disagreement handling is limited.

Investigation.t: Interview: Finding out a school community member's story first-hand
Investigation.y: Students interview a real person live in Tamil, ask their own questions and make sense of the replies to build the article. They find out first-hand.

Conclusion.t: Video and reflection: Sharing the story found and reflecting on it
Conclusion.y: Groups share what they found in a recorded presentation and write an individual reflection in class on the project.

Engagement.t: Newspaper article: Choosing an interviewee and making an own product
Engagement.y: Groups choose their own interviewee from the school community and make a newspaper article and video that they own.

Accomplishment.t: Newspaper article: Drafting, peer editing and reflecting
Accomplishment.y: Groups draft the article, peer-edit it and revise before submission, then each writes an individual reflection on the work.

3.label: Chinese (CL)
3.title: Recorded opinion video
3.format: Video of 1 to 2 minutes giving a view on a school issue with at least two reasons; 10 marks. Individual.
3.builds: Builds on Term 2 oral practice in sharing a view with reasons.

CCI 1.t: Give a view, two reasons and what I would do
CCI 1.y: Students record a short video stating a view, at least two reasons and their own action. Marks go to content, expression, structure and timing. One way only.

3.label: Chinese (CL)
3.title: Three minutes to persuade you: group argumentative video
3.format: Group of 2 to 3 writes an argumentative text then records a 3 to 4 minute video on a set school issue (50 marks: content and structure 20 group, expression 20 individual, video quality 5, creativity 5).
3.when: Term 3: groups formed Wk2, final text Wk5, video submitted 11 Aug 2026.
3.builds: Builds on the argumentative writing unit (introduction, body, conclusion) and PEEL.

CCI 1.t: Persuade a school audience with credible evidence
CCI 1.y: Groups write an argument with PEEL, quotation and example, then deliver it persuasively in video, judging which evidence is credible and representative.

Conceptualisation.t: Take a stance and outline the argument
Conceptualisation.y: Students take a stance on the issue and outline introduction, body and conclusion before researching.

Investigation.y: Students search for data and examples, record links and dates, and compare sources for credibility and representativeness.

Conclusion.t: Turn the argument into video and take peer evaluation
Conclusion.y: Groups convert the written argument to a spoken video and take part in a mid-task peer evaluation.

Accomplishment.t: Peer evaluation against the rubric mid-task
Accomplishment.y: Groups receive peer evaluation against the given rubric before the final video.

3.label: Chinese (CL)
3.title: Campus video station: group argumentative video
3.format: Group records a 3.5 to 4 minute argumentative video with a script (50 marks: content, language and structure 20, expression 20, video quality, creativity and script 10).
3.builds: Builds on argumentative writing with PEEL, quotation and example.

CCI 1.t: Argue a stance from three angles with reliable sources
CCI 1.y: The rubric rewards a clear stance argued from three angles, two types of reliable source, PEEL, and confident delivery to camera. Based on the rubric only; the task sheet was not found.

3.label: Chinese (CL)
3.title: Campus current-affairs news video
3.format: Group of 4 records a 5 to 7 minute news or current-affairs video taking a stance on a chosen issue, with a written argument (50 marks: argument 20 group, expression 20 individual, collaboration and production 10).
3.builds: Builds on the argumentative writing unit and the three argument methods (example, quotation, contrast).

CCI 1.t: Present a stance as a news programme
CCI 1.y: Groups argue a stance with three argument methods in an interactive news style for an audience.

CGC 1.t: Analyse at least two views on a community issue
CGC 1.y: Groups pick an issue such as hawker food, plastic use or student stress, analyse at least two viewpoints and then take a stance.

Conceptualisation.y: Groups pick one issue from a list, or propose their own for approval, and fix a stance.

Investigation.t: Gather reliable evidence and interview content
Investigation.y: Groups collect information, filter reliable arguments and add interview content to the script.

Conclusion.t: Present the stance as a news video
Conclusion.y: Groups record and share the news-style video.

Engagement.y: Groups choose from paired statements or propose their own with approval.

3.label: Malay (ML)
3.title: WA3 team debate
3.format: Team debate on a given motion: group keyword definitions and main ideas, individual script, spoken delivery with rebuttal and interjection, and a team strategy mark.
3.builds: Sec 1 and 2 oral presentation skills and Sec 3 reasoning, giving explanation and examples for an opinion.

CCI 1.t: WA3 authentic task: team debate on a school or youth motion, with prepared scripts
CCI 1.y: Teams argue a stated side of a motion in set speaking roles, with key terms defined, main ideas for both sides listed, and rebuttal or interjection in response to opponents. Scored on team strategy too.

3.label: Tamil (TL)
3.title: Debate: Singapore youths and ancient Tamil cultural customs
3.format: Team debate in Tamil with equal for and against speakers. G1 teams of 6, G2 pairs, G3 teams of 4 recorded as a video, HTL teams of 4 live in class. Each speaker gives reasons, evidence and rebuttal.
3.builds: The G1 and G2 prep form gives frames for reason and evidence; no unit is named.

CCI 1.t: Debate speech: Arguing a position with reasons and evidence
CCI 1.y: Students prepare and deliver a debate speech of about 2 to 3 minutes with reasons and evidence, and rebut the other side. Spoken to a class audience.

CGC 1.t: Debate: Whether Singapore youths still keep ancient Tamil customs
CGC 1.y: Students argue for or against whether Singapore youths still keep ancient Tamil cultural customs, drawing on themes such as food. The topic is about Singapore culture, with both sides heard.
